These pathways indicate that oxybenzone may influence the function of SLC1B3 through indirect mechanisms, possibly by modulating the activity of upstream targets. The scores from the paths suggest a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, with varying degrees of support from different molecular interactions. The evidence highlights the possibility that oxybenzone could act as a modulator of SLC1B3 through a network of downstream targets, though the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated. The integration of these pathways underscores the complexity of the relationship and the need for further experimental validation to confirm the direct interaction between oxybenzone and SLC1B3.
